title: Generative AI Mastery: Build LLM Apps, RAG & Agents with Python
subtitle: Go from basic Python to deployed GenAI apps: LLM APIs, structured output, RAG with citations, safe agents, evals and a portfolio for GenAI roles.
description:
This is a hands-on engineering course for people who already write basic Python and want to build real applications on top of large language models. You will not just chat with an AI tool; you will call LLM APIs from code, get validated structured data out of them, connect them to your own documents and tools, and deploy the result.

You start with how LLMs work from an engineer's point of view: tokens, context windows, sampling and embeddings. Then you build steadily: a streaming CLI chatbot, a Streamlit web app, a GST invoice extraction API with Pydantic validation, a document Q&A system with retrieval and citations, and a tool-using agent that analyses CSV data with a safe calculator. Along the way you learn evaluation with test sets, prompt caching and cost control, prompt-injection and PII defences, retries, Docker and cloud deployment.

Examples use Python and the Anthropic Claude API, with notes on how the same patterns apply to OpenAI, Gemini and open-source models via Ollama. Every lesson is written for Indian learners, with local examples such as GST invoices, UPI, HR policies and Naukri job hunting, and ends with a 10-20 minute exercise.

The final module turns your work into a deployed portfolio project with a strong README and prepares you for GenAI interviews in India: concept questions, coding rounds and system design.
audience: Software developers who want to move into GenAI engineering roles
CS/IT students and recent graduates building a job-ready AI portfolio
Engineers in Indian IT services companies joining GenAI projects or practices
Data analysts comfortable with Python who want to build LLM-powered tools
Freelancers who want to offer RAG, chatbot and document automation projects
outcomes: Explain tokens, context windows, sampling and embeddings clearly in interviews and design reviews
Call LLM APIs from Python with system prompts, multi-turn history, streaming and error handling
Extract validated JSON from text, PDFs and images using structured output and Pydantic
Build tool-calling apps and agents with step limits, approval gates and safe tools
Build a RAG pipeline with chunking, vector search, grounded answers and page-level citations
Evaluate RAG and prompts with test sets, retrieval hit rate and LLM-as-judge grading
Reduce cost with prompt caching, effort settings and model routing, and defend against prompt injection
Deploy LLM apps with Docker and environment variables, and present them as a portfolio project
prerequisites: Basic Python: functions, lists and dictionaries, loops, and reading files
Comfort installing packages with pip and using virtual environments
A laptop that can run Python 3.10+ and an LLM API account (usage is billed by the provider)
projects: A document Q&A (RAG) app that answers only from your PDFs and cites the file and page for every claim.
A GST invoice extraction API that turns PDFs and photos into validated JSON and flags invoices needing review.
A data analyst agent that answers questions over a sales CSV using safe aggregation tools and a calculator.
A deployed portfolio demo with Docker, a public URL, evaluation results and a recruiter-ready README.

faqs.q: How much Python do I need before starting?
faqs.a: You should be comfortable writing functions, working with lists and dictionaries, installing packages with pip and using a virtual environment. You do not need prior machine learning experience; the course explains the LLM concepts you need from scratch.

faqs.q: Will I have to pay for an LLM API?
faqs.a: Yes, the examples call a paid API, which the provider bills by usage. For the exercises in this course the usage is typically modest, and the course teaches you to measure tokens and control cost. Check the provider's current pricing before you start.

faqs.q: Is this course only about Claude, or will it help with OpenAI and Gemini too?
faqs.a: Code examples use the Anthropic Claude API so that everything is consistent and runnable. The patterns (messages, structured output, tool calling, streaming, RAG, evaluation) are the same across providers, and lessons point out how they map to OpenAI, Gemini and open-source models via Ollama.

faqs.q: Will this course guarantee me a GenAI job?
faqs.a: No course can guarantee a job. What it gives you is practical skills, four portfolio projects including a deployed one, and structured interview preparation, which together make you a much stronger candidate for GenAI and AI engineer roles.
Yes. A certificate of completion is issued once you mark every lesson in the course as complete.
